captions.text: If you look at the absolute I mean the
absolute Shakespearean tragedy that played out in Silicon Valley
during the 2010s between Microsoft and Google, you
quickly realize a really fundamental counterintuitive
truth and that is competition is for losers.
Yeah. Literally. Like it's not healthy.
It's not a driver of ultimate value and it
completely blinds you. You had these two tech behemoths.
Right. Right. They started out in entirely different universes.
Exactly. I mean, Microsoft was the undisputed
dominant king of operating systems and, you know,
desktop office And Google was
this pure algorithm-driven search engine focused
entirely on the internet.
There was absolutely zero structural reason for them to
ever cross paths or step on each other's toes.
Not at all. But as they grew, instead of
looking at new frontiers, they became completely and
inexplicably obsessed with each other.
It just became this massive expensive street fight.
It really was. It was Windows versus Chrome OS.
It was Bing versus Google Search.
